do_more: Keep runtime around 30‑45 seconds – use micro (≈30s) for simple jokes and standard (≈42s) for deeper concepts
Open with a vivid, relatable scenario that shows the problem within the first 3‑5 seconds
Title the video as a concise, curiosity‑driven phrase naming a specific bias or trap (e.g., “The Confidence Curve”) and omit emojis
Use exaggerated visual comedy to illustrate the psychological idea, then deliver a punchy takeaway
Add a single, clear call‑to‑action (e.g., “Ever felt this? Comment below”)
avoid: Generic “Your ___” titles that rely on emojis or filler words
Repeating the same hook pattern across episodes (e.g., “Your ___ Panic”)
Long intros or slow builds that delay the joke beyond 5 seconds
Overly abstract titles that don’t name a concrete concept
short.title_style: Use a concise, curiosity‑driven phrase that names a specific psychological bias or trap (e.g., “The Confidence Curve”) without emojis or filler
next_tests: A/B test titles: “The ___ Trap” vs. “Why ___ Happens” for the same video
